1.summary: Jacob's descendants multiply in Egypt until a new Pharaoh who didn't know Joseph enslaves them; when forced labor fails to stop their growth, he orders the Hebrew midwives to kill newborn boys, but they fear God and refuse, so Pharaoh orders every Hebrew boy thrown into the Nile.
1.lookfor: Notice how Israel's growth fulfills God's promise, and the courage of the midwives.

names.name: Pharaoh
names.gloss: Egypt's king, who did not know Joseph.

names.name: Pithom
names.gloss: A store city in the Nile delta.

names.name: Raamses
names.gloss: A store city, probably the royal city of Rameses II.

names.name: Shiphrah
names.gloss: A Hebrew midwife who defied Pharaoh.

names.name: Puah
names.gloss: The other midwife.

insights.title: Fruitful and multiplied
insights.body: The children of Israel were fruitful, increased abundantly, multiplied and grew exceedingly mighty (1:7). The language of creation and of God's promise to Abraham is coming true.

insights.title: Who didn't know Joseph
insights.body: A new king arose who didn't know Joseph (1:8). Generations pass; gratitude is forgotten, and the protected family becomes a threatened minority.

insights.title: Store cities
insights.body: Israel built the store cities Pithom and Raamses (1:11). Egyptian records describe foreign laborers making bricks for Rameses II's building projects in the delta.

insights.title: The more they afflicted them
insights.body: The more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and spread (1:12). Oppression can't stop God's purpose.

insights.title: The midwives feared God
insights.body: Shiphrah and Puah feared God and didn't do what the king commanded (1:17). Two women are named in the story; the mighty Pharaoh isn't. History remembers the faithful.

insights.title: God made them households
insights.body: Because the midwives feared God, he gave them families (1:21). God honors those who honor him.

insights.title: Into the river
insights.body: Every son born you shall cast into the river (1:22). The Nile, Egypt's source of life, becomes an instrument of death. The next chapter shows how God turns it around.

insights.title: Quiet courage
insights.body: The midwives resisted evil quietly, at great risk. Where might God be asking you to quietly refuse to go along with wrong?

2.summary: A Levite woman hides her baby boy, then places him in a basket in the reeds of the Nile; Pharaoh's daughter finds and adopts him, naming him Moses; grown, Moses kills an Egyptian beating a Hebrew and flees to Midian, where he marries Zipporah; meanwhile God hears Israel's groaning and remembers his covenant.
2.lookfor: Notice the women who save Moses, and the last four verses, where God hears, remembers, sees and knows.

names.name: Levi
names.gloss: The tribe of Moses' parents.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: The baby drawn out of the water, Israel's future deliverer.

names.name: Midian
names.gloss: A desert region east of the Gulf of Aqaba.

names.name: Reuel
names.gloss: A priest of Midian, also called Jethro, Moses' father-in-law.

names.name: Zipporah
names.gloss: Reuel's daughter, Moses' wife.

names.name: Gershom
names.gloss: Moses' son; the name sounds like a stranger there.

insights.title: An ark
insights.body: The mother puts the baby in a papyrus basket coated with tar (2:3). The Hebrew word, tevah, is the same as Noah's ark: God again saves a future through a small floating box.

insights.title: Women who saved him
insights.body: His mother, his sister, Pharaoh's daughter and her servants all play a part (2:2-10). Pharaoh's own daughter rescues the child Pharaoh ordered killed.

insights.title: Moses
insights.body: She named him Moses, because I drew him out of the water (2:10). In Egyptian, mose means son, as in Rameses; in Hebrew it sounds like drawing out. He will draw Israel out through water.

insights.title: Moses' first attempt
insights.body: Moses kills an Egyptian taskmaster and hides him in the sand (2:12). Right instinct, wrong method; he acts alone and has to flee. Stephen says he supposed his brothers would understand that God would rescue them through him.

insights.title: At a well
insights.body: In Midian, Moses defends seven sisters at a well and marries one of them (2:16-21). Like Rebekah and Rachel, a marriage begins at a well.

insights.title: God heard, remembered, saw, knew
insights.body: God heard their groaning, remembered his covenant, saw the children of Israel, and knew (2:24-25). Four verbs: before God acts, he cares.

insights.title: Waiting
insights.body: Moses spent forty years in the desert before God called him. What might God be preparing in you during a season that feels like waiting?

3.summary: Tending sheep at Horeb, Moses sees a bush that burns but isn't consumed; God calls to him from it, tells him to remove his sandals, reveals that he has seen Israel's misery and will rescue them, sends Moses to Pharaoh, and reveals his name: I AM WHO I AM, Yahweh.
3.lookfor: Notice Moses' objections and God's answers, and the meaning of God's name.

names.name: Jethro
names.gloss: Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian.

names.name: Horeb
names.gloss: The mountain of God, also called Sinai.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: An eighty-year-old shepherd, called by God.

insights.title: A bush not burned up
insights.body: The bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed (3:2). God's presence like fire, yet not destroying.

insights.title: Take off your sandals
insights.body: Take off your sandals, for the place where you stand is holy ground (3:5). Removing sandals was a sign of respect; priests later served barefoot in the sanctuary.

insights.title: I have seen
insights.body: I have surely seen the affliction of my people, heard their cry, and I know their sorrows; I have come down to deliver them (3:7-8). God sees, hears, knows and comes down.

insights.title: Who am I?
insights.body: Moses asks, who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh? God doesn't answer the question about Moses; he says, certainly I will be with you (3:11-12). The answer to who am I is who God is.

insights.title: I AM
insights.body: I AM WHO I AM (3:14). God's name Yahweh is related to the Hebrew verb to be: the self-existent, ever-present one. Jesus said, before Abraham was, I AM.

insights.title: The God of your fathers
insights.body: I am the God of Abraham, of Isaac and of Jacob (3:6). Jesus quoted this to show that God's people live to him: he is not the God of the dead but of the living.

insights.title: A land flowing with milk and honey
insights.body: God promises to bring them to a good and large land, flowing with milk and honey (3:8). Milk from flocks and honey from wild bees or dates: abundance without irrigation.

insights.title: Holy ground
insights.body: God met Moses in the middle of ordinary work. Where in your everyday routine might God be calling you to stop and pay attention?

4.summary: Moses objects that the people won't believe him, so God gives him signs: a staff that becomes a snake, a hand made leprous and healed, and water turned to blood; when Moses says he isn't eloquent, God angrily appoints Aaron to speak for him; Moses returns to Egypt, and the elders believe and worship.
4.lookfor: Notice Moses' excuses and God's patience, then anger, and the strange episode on the way.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Moses' older brother, a gifted speaker.

names.name: Zipporah
names.gloss: Moses' wife, who circumcised their son.

names.name: Jethro
names.gloss: Moses' father-in-law, who lets him go.

insights.title: What's in your hand?
insights.body: God asks, what is that in your hand? A rod (4:2). A shepherd's ordinary staff becomes the staff of God (4:20). God uses what we already have.

insights.title: Snakes
insights.body: The rod becomes a serpent (4:3). The cobra was a symbol of Pharaoh's power, worn on his crown. Moses grasping the snake by its tail pictures mastery over Pharaoh.

insights.title: Slow of speech
insights.body: I am slow of speech and of tongue (4:10). God replies, who made man's mouth? (4:11). Inadequacy isn't an excuse when God is the one sending.

insights.title: Please send someone else
insights.body: Moses finally says, please send someone else, and Yahweh's anger burns (4:13-14). Yet God provides Aaron. God's patience includes concessions to our weakness.

insights.title: My firstborn son
insights.body: Israel is my son, my firstborn; let my son go, or I will kill your firstborn son (4:22-23). The plagues end where this begins: God fights for his children.

insights.title: The bridegroom of blood
insights.body: On the way, Yahweh meets Moses and seeks to kill him, until Zipporah circumcises their son (4:24-26). A puzzling scene; it seems Moses had neglected the covenant sign, and the leader must keep it himself.

insights.title: They bowed and worshiped
insights.body: When the people heard that Yahweh had seen their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshiped (4:31). Hope arrives before rescue.

insights.title: Excuses
insights.body: Moses had five excuses for not going. What excuses do you make when you sense God calling you?

5.summary: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel go to worship; Pharaoh refuses, saying he doesn't know Yahweh, and orders the slaves to gather their own straw while making the same number of bricks; the beaten foremen blame Moses, and Moses complains to God.
5.lookfor: Notice Pharaoh's question, and how things get worse before they get better.

names.name: Pharaoh
names.gloss: Who says, who is Yahweh?

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: Discouraged after his first attempt.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Moses' spokesman.

insights.title: Who is Yahweh?
insights.body: Who is Yahweh, that I should listen to his voice? I don't know Yahweh (5:2). The whole story of the plagues answers this question: so that you may know that I am Yahweh.

insights.title: Bricks and straw
insights.body: Egyptian mud bricks were mixed with straw to bind them. Making the slaves gather their own straw while keeping the same quota (5:7-8) was a calculated cruelty. Egyptian papyri record brick quotas for laborers.

insights.title: Lies
insights.body: Pharaoh says they're idle, and asks why they listen to lying words (5:8-9). The oppressor calls the cry for freedom laziness.

insights.title: Serve
insights.body: Let my people go, that they may hold a feast, or serve, me (5:1). The Hebrew word for work, slavery and worship is the same, avad. The question of Exodus: whom will Israel serve?

insights.title: You made us stink
insights.body: The foremen tell Moses and Aaron, you have made us stink in Pharaoh's eyes (5:21). Moses' first obedience makes everything worse.

insights.title: Why have you brought trouble?
insights.body: Moses asks Yahweh, why have you brought trouble on this people? You haven't rescued them at all (5:22-23). An honest complaint prayer, and God answers it in chapter 6.

insights.title: When it gets worse
insights.body: Things got worse right after Moses obeyed. How do you keep trusting God when doing the right thing seems to backfire?

6.summary: God answers Moses by restating his name and covenant: he will bring Israel out, redeem them with an outstretched arm, take them as his people and bring them into the land; the people, crushed by slavery, won't listen; a genealogy of Moses and Aaron follows.
6.lookfor: Notice the series of I will promises in verses 6 to 8, and why the people can't listen.

names.name: Amram
names.gloss: Moses and Aaron's father.

names.name: Jochebed
names.gloss: Moses and Aaron's mother.

names.name: Elisheba
names.gloss: Aaron's wife.

names.name: Nadab
names.gloss: Aaron's son.

names.name: Eleazar
names.gloss: Aaron's son, later high priest.

names.name: Phinehas
names.gloss: Eleazar's son.

names.name: Korah
names.gloss: Moses' cousin, who later rebelled.

skim.advice: Verses 14 to 25 are a genealogy of Moses and Aaron; skim the names.

insights.title: By my name Yahweh
insights.body: I appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as God Almighty, but by my name Yahweh I wasn't known to them (6:3). The patriarchs used the name, but now Israel will know its meaning through what God does.

insights.title: Seven I wills
insights.body: I will bring you out, I will rid you of bondage, I will redeem you, I will take you as my people, I will be your God, I will bring you into the land, I will give it to you (6:6-8). The whole plan of rescue in God's own words.

insights.title: Four cups
insights.body: Jewish tradition links the four cups of wine at the Passover meal to four of these promises: bring out, deliver, redeem, take. Jesus' cup of the new covenant at the Last Supper was likely one of these.

insights.title: Redeem
insights.body: I will redeem you with an outstretched arm (6:6). A redeemer was a family member who paid to free a relative from slavery or debt. God acts as Israel's next of kin.

insights.title: Anguish of spirit
insights.body: They didn't listen to Moses because of anguish of spirit and cruel bondage (6:9). Trauma can make hope hard to hear. God doesn't give up on them.

insights.title: Uncircumcised lips
insights.body: Moses says, I have uncircumcised lips (6:12), a vivid way of saying he speaks poorly. God sends him anyway.

insights.title: Hard to hear
insights.body: Israel couldn't hear hope because of their pain. Is there someone whose pain makes it hard for them to hear good news, whom you could patiently care for?

7.summary: God sends Moses, now eighty, and Aaron, eighty-three, to Pharaoh, warning that Pharaoh's heart will be hardened so that Egypt will know Yahweh; Aaron's staff becomes a serpent and swallows the magicians' staffs; then the first plague turns the Nile and all Egypt's water to blood, but the magicians copy it and Pharaoh's heart stays hard.
7.lookfor: Notice the purpose of the plagues, and the contest with Egypt's magicians.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: Who was eighty years old.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Whose staff swallowed the magicians'.

names.name: Pharaoh
names.gloss: Whose heart was hardened.

insights.title: As God to Pharaoh
insights.body: I have made you as God to Pharaoh, and Aaron will be your prophet (7:1). Moses speaks for God; Aaron speaks for Moses.

insights.title: Hardened hearts
insights.body: The text says both that Pharaoh hardened his heart and that God hardened it (7:13, 8:15, 9:12). Pharaoh's stubbornness is his own, and God confirms it. Paul discusses this in Romans 9.

insights.title: That Egypt may know
insights.body: The Egyptians will know that I am Yahweh (7:5). The plagues aren't only punishment; they reveal who God is, to Egypt and to Israel.

insights.title: The magicians
insights.body: Egypt's wise men and sorcerers copy the first signs with their secret arts (7:11). Paul names two of them from Jewish tradition: Jannes and Jambres.

insights.title: Swallowed
insights.body: Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods (7:12). The serpent symbol of Pharaoh's power is swallowed by God's.

insights.title: The Nile to blood
insights.body: The Nile, worshiped as a source of life and linked to the god Hapi, turns to blood (7:20). Pharaoh used it to drown Hebrew babies; now it becomes death to Egypt.

insights.title: Against all Egypt's gods
insights.body: God later says, against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments (12:12). Each plague strikes something Egypt trusted: the river, the land, the sky, the sun.

insights.title: Hardening
insights.body: Pharaoh's heart grew harder each time he refused. Is there an area where you keep saying no to God, and your heart may be hardening?

8.summary: God sends frogs over Egypt, and Pharaoh begs for relief but hardens his heart once they die; then lice, which the magicians can't copy, calling it the finger of God; then swarms of flies, which spare Goshen where Israel lives; Pharaoh bargains and again refuses.
8.lookfor: Notice the magicians' confession, and the distinction God makes between Egypt and Israel.

names.name: Goshen
names.gloss: The region where Israel lived, spared from the flies.

names.name: Pharaoh
names.gloss: Who bargains and breaks his word.

insights.title: Frogs
insights.body: Frogs fill homes, beds and ovens (8:3). Egyptians associated frogs with Heqet, a goddess of fertility and birth; now they become a plague.

insights.title: Tomorrow
insights.body: Asked when he wants the frogs gone, Pharaoh says, tomorrow (8:10). One more night with the frogs rather than humble himself today.

insights.title: The finger of God
insights.body: When they can't produce lice, the magicians tell Pharaoh, this is the finger of God (8:19). Jesus used the same phrase: if I cast out demons by the finger of God, the kingdom has come.

insights.title: A distinction
insights.body: I will set apart the land of Goshen, where my people live, so that no swarms of flies will be there (8:22). From here on, the plagues distinguish between God's people and Egypt.

insights.title: Bargaining
insights.body: Pharaoh offers: sacrifice to your God in the land; then, you may go, but not very far (8:25, 8:28). Half-measures that keep Israel under his control.

insights.title: An abomination to Egypt
insights.body: Moses replies that their sacrifices would be an abomination to the Egyptians (8:26), likely because animals sacred to Egyptians would be offered.

insights.title: Broken promises
insights.body: Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also (8:32). Relief leads not to gratitude but to renewed stubbornness.

insights.title: Tomorrow
insights.body: Pharaoh chose one more night with the frogs. What are you putting off until tomorrow that God is asking of you today?

9.summary: A plague kills Egypt's livestock but spares Israel's; boils break out on people and animals, even the magicians; God warns of the worst hail ever, and some of Pharaoh's officials believe and shelter their servants and animals; hail strikes Egypt but not Goshen; Pharaoh admits he has sinned, then hardens his heart again.
9.lookfor: Notice the Egyptians who feared God's word, and Pharaoh's shallow confession.

names.name: Goshen
names.gloss: Spared from the hail.

names.name: Pharaoh
names.gloss: Who confessed but didn't change.

insights.title: Livestock
insights.body: Disease kills Egypt's horses, donkeys, camels, cattle and sheep (9:3). Egyptians revered several animals, including the Apis bull, as sacred.

insights.title: The magicians couldn't stand
insights.body: The magicians couldn't stand before Moses because of the boils (9:11). Pharaoh's experts are now among the afflicted.

insights.title: For this purpose
insights.body: For this cause I have raised you up, to show you my power, and that my name may be declared through all the earth (9:16). Paul quotes this in Romans to speak of God's sovereignty.

insights.title: He who feared the word
insights.body: Those among Pharaoh's servants who feared Yahweh's word brought their servants and livestock inside (9:20). Some Egyptians believed; the line between God's people and others begins to blur.

insights.title: I have sinned this time
insights.body: Pharaoh says, I have sinned this time; Yahweh is righteous, and I and my people are wicked (9:27). Words of repentance without a change of heart.

insights.title: The earth is Yahweh's
insights.body: Moses will spread his hands and the hail will stop, so you may know that the earth is Yahweh's (9:29).

insights.title: Hail and harvest
insights.body: The flax and barley were ruined, but wheat and spelt were not, because they ripen later (9:31-32). Exact seasonal detail: barley and flax ripen around February-March in Egypt.

insights.title: Words or change
insights.body: Pharaoh said the right words but didn't change. Is there anything you've confessed to God but not yet turned from?

10.summary: Pharaoh's officials beg him to let Israel go, but he will release only the men; locusts devour everything the hail left; then darkness covers Egypt for three days, though Israel has light; Pharaoh offers to let the people go without their flocks, Moses refuses, and Pharaoh threatens him with death.
10.lookfor: Notice Pharaoh's officials turning against him, and the darkness that is felt.

names.name: Pharaoh
names.gloss: Whose servants say Egypt is destroyed.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: Who refuses to leave even a hoof behind.

insights.title: Tell your children
insights.body: God says the plagues are so that you may tell your son and grandson what I have done in Egypt (10:2). The story is meant to be passed down.

insights.title: Egypt is destroyed
insights.body: Pharaoh's servants say, how long will this man be a snare to us? Don't you know Egypt is destroyed? (10:7). Even his advisers see what he refuses to.

insights.title: Only the men
insights.body: Pharaoh offers to let only the men go (10:11), keeping wives and children as hostages. Moses insists everyone must go: young and old, sons and daughters.

insights.title: Locusts
insights.body: Locusts covered the surface of the whole earth so that the land was dark (10:15). Joel later described a locust plague as an army of God's judgment.

insights.title: Darkness felt
insights.body: Darkness which may be felt covers Egypt for three days (10:21-22). The sun god Ra was Egypt's chief deity; now the sun itself is hidden.

insights.title: Light in their homes
insights.body: All the children of Israel had light in their dwellings (10:23). God's people live in light while the world around them is dark.

insights.title: Not a hoof
insights.body: Not a hoof shall be left behind (10:26). Total deliverance: God won't settle for a partial exodus.

insights.title: Light in darkness
insights.body: Israel had light while Egypt sat in darkness. Where is God giving you light in a dark situation?

11.summary: God tells Moses one last plague is coming, after which Pharaoh will drive Israel out; the Israelites ask their Egyptian neighbors for silver and gold and receive it; Moses warns Pharaoh that at midnight every firstborn in Egypt will die, but not a dog will bark against Israel, and leaves in hot anger.
11.lookfor: Notice the favor Israel has with Egypt's people, and the distinction between Egypt and Israel.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: Very great in the land of Egypt.

names.name: Pharaoh
names.gloss: Who will not listen.

insights.title: Silver and gold
insights.body: Let every man ask his neighbor for jewels of silver and gold (11:2). God had promised Abraham his descendants would leave with great possessions. These would later be given for the tabernacle.

insights.title: Very great
insights.body: The man Moses was very great in Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and the people (11:3). The fugitive has become a respected figure even among the enemy.

insights.title: The firstborn
insights.body: All the firstborn in Egypt will die, from Pharaoh's firstborn to the firstborn of the slave girl (11:5). Pharaoh had killed Israel's sons; God warned at the start that Pharaoh's firstborn would answer for Israel, God's firstborn.

insights.title: A great cry
insights.body: There will be a great cry throughout Egypt, such as there has never been (11:6). Israel's cry went up from slavery; now Egypt cries.

insights.title: Not a dog
insights.body: Against Israel not even a dog will bark (11:7). Total peace for God's people on the night of judgment, so Egypt may know that Yahweh makes a distinction.

insights.title: Hot anger
insights.body: Moses went out from Pharaoh in hot anger (11:8). The meek Moses is angry at the hardness that will cost so many lives.

insights.title: Favor
insights.body: God gave Israel favor even with their oppressors. Where have you seen God give you unexpected favor?

12.summary: God institutes the Passover: each household is to kill a spotless lamb, put its blood on the doorposts and eat it in haste with unleavened bread and bitter herbs; at midnight Yahweh strikes Egypt's firstborn but passes over the houses marked by blood; Pharaoh drives Israel out, and they leave after 430 years, with a mixed multitude.
12.lookfor: Notice the details of the meal, the meaning of the blood, and the command to remember.

names.name: Rameses
names.gloss: The city from which Israel set out.

names.name: Succoth
names.gloss: Israel's first stop after leaving Egypt.

insights.title: A new calendar
insights.body: This month will be the beginning of months for you (12:2). The exodus resets Israel's calendar: freedom is year one.

insights.title: Without blemish
insights.body: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male a year old (12:5). Peter says we were redeemed by the precious blood of Christ, like a lamb without blemish.

insights.title: Pass over
insights.body: When I see the blood, I will pass over you (12:13). The Hebrew pesach gives us Passover. The blood marks the household that trusts God's word.

insights.title: Eaten in haste
insights.body: Eat it with your belt fastened, sandals on your feet and staff in your hand, in haste (12:11). Unleavened bread, because there was no time for the dough to rise.

insights.title: Not a bone broken
insights.body: You shall not break any of its bones (12:46). John notes that the soldiers didn't break Jesus' legs, fulfilling this.

insights.title: When your children ask
insights.body: When your children ask, what do you mean by this service? you shall say, it's the sacrifice of Yahweh's Passover (12:26-27). The Passover meal is built around children's questions; Jews still keep it this way.

insights.title: A mixed multitude
insights.body: A mixed multitude went up with them (12:38). Not only Israelites left Egypt; others joined, and the law makes room for foreigners who keep the Passover.

insights.title: The Lord's Supper
insights.body: Jesus ate the Passover with his disciples the night he was betrayed and gave it new meaning: the bread his body, the cup the new covenant in his blood.

insights.title: Under the blood
insights.body: Israel's safety depended on the lamb's blood, not their own goodness. What does it mean for you to trust in Christ, our Passover?

13.summary: God commands that every firstborn be dedicated to him and that the Feast of Unleavened Bread be kept as a memorial; God leads Israel not by the short road through Philistine territory but by the wilderness toward the Red Sea; Moses takes Joseph's bones; Yahweh goes before them in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.
13.lookfor: Notice why God takes the long way, and the pillar that never leaves.

names.name: Philistines
names.gloss: Peoples along the coast, on the direct road to Canaan.

names.name: Joseph
names.gloss: Whose bones Israel carried out of Egypt.

names.name: Etham
names.gloss: A camp at the edge of the wilderness.

insights.title: Dedicating the firstborn
insights.body: Sanctify to me all the firstborn (13:2). Since God spared Israel's firstborn, they belong to him. Firstborn sons were redeemed with an offering, as Mary and Joseph did for Jesus.

insights.title: On your hand and forehead
insights.body: It shall be for a sign on your hand and a memorial between your eyes (13:9). Later, Jewish men took this literally, wearing small boxes containing Scripture called tefillin.

insights.title: The long way
insights.body: God didn't lead them by the way of the Philistines, though it was near, lest the people change their minds when they see war (13:17). The shortest road isn't always God's road.

insights.title: Joseph's bones
insights.body: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, as Joseph had made Israel swear (13:19). A promise made 400 years earlier is kept.

insights.title: Pillar of cloud and fire
insights.body: Yahweh went before them by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire (13:21). God's visible presence leads them every step.

insights.title: Never removed
insights.body: The pillar of cloud by day and fire by night didn't depart from before the people (13:22). Constant guidance, day and night.

insights.title: The long way round
insights.body: God led Israel the long way to protect them. Where might God be leading you a longer way for your own good?

14.summary: God leads Israel to camp by the sea, and Pharaoh pursues with chariots; the terrified people cry out against Moses, who tells them to stand still and see Yahweh's salvation; the pillar moves behind them, Moses stretches out his hand, an east wind divides the sea, Israel crosses on dry ground, and the waters return over Egypt's army.
14.lookfor: Notice Moses' words in verses 13 and 14, and what the people do at the end.

names.name: Pihahiroth
names.gloss: A camp by the sea, location uncertain.

names.name: Migdol
names.gloss: A tower or fort near the camp.

names.name: Baal Zephon
names.gloss: A place named after a Canaanite god of the north.

insights.title: A trap
insights.body: God tells Israel to turn back and camp by the sea, so Pharaoh will think they are trapped (14:2-3). God sets the stage for a final victory.

insights.title: Better to serve Egypt
insights.body: The people say, weren't there graves in Egypt, that you brought us to die in the wilderness? It's better to serve the Egyptians (14:11-12). Fear makes slavery look safe.

insights.title: Stand still
insights.body: Don't be afraid, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh; Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still (14:13-14). The first use in the Bible of the word salvation for God's rescue of his people.

insights.title: Go forward
insights.body: Yet God also tells Moses, why do you cry to me? Tell the people to go forward (14:15). Stillness of trust, then steps of faith.

insights.title: The Red Sea
insights.body: The Hebrew name is Yam Suph, sea of reeds (14:2). Scholars debate its location: the Gulf of Suez, the Bitter Lakes, or a marshy lake in the delta. The story stresses that a strong east wind all night divided it.

insights.title: Baptized in the sea
insights.body: Israel walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on each side (14:22). Paul says they were baptized into Moses in the cloud and the sea.

insights.title: Feared and believed
insights.body: Israel saw the great work, feared Yahweh, and believed in Yahweh and in his servant Moses (14:31). Rescue leads to faith.

insights.title: Between the army and the sea
insights.body: Israel was trapped between Pharaoh's army and the sea when God made a way. Where do you feel trapped, and what would trusting God to fight for you look like?

15.summary: Moses and Israel sing a song celebrating Yahweh's victory at the sea and his leading them to his holy dwelling, and Miriam leads the women with tambourines; three days later at Marah the water is bitter, Moses throws in a tree and it becomes sweet, and God promises to be their healer; they camp at Elim with its springs and palms.
15.lookfor: Notice how the song praises who God is, and how quickly the people grumble afterward.

names.name: Miriam
names.gloss: Moses' sister, a prophetess.

names.name: Marah
names.gloss: A place of bitter water; the name means bitter.

names.name: Elim
names.gloss: An oasis with twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

names.name: Philistia
names.gloss: The coastal land of the Philistines.

names.name: Edom
names.gloss: The nation descended from Esau.

insights.title: One of the oldest poems
insights.body: The Song of the Sea (15:1-18) is considered by many scholars one of the oldest pieces of poetry in the Bible, with archaic Hebrew forms.

insights.title: My strength and song
insights.body: Yahweh is my strength and song, and he has become my salvation (15:2). The same words are sung in Psalm 118 and Isaiah 12.

insights.title: A man of war
insights.body: Yahweh is a man of war; Yahweh is his name (15:3). Israel didn't fight; God fought for them.

insights.title: Who is like you?
insights.body: Who is like you, Yahweh, among the gods? Who is like you, glorious in holiness? (15:11). Revelation's song of Moses and the Lamb echoes it.

insights.title: Miriam's song
insights.body: Miriam the prophetess took a tambourine, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and dances (15:20). She is the first woman called a prophetess in the Bible.

insights.title: Three days later
insights.body: Three days after the sea, at Marah, the people grumble about bitter water (15:24). The song fades fast when thirst comes.

insights.title: Yahweh who heals
insights.body: I am Yahweh who heals you (15:26). God sweetens the bitter water and reveals himself as healer.

insights.title: From song to grumble
insights.body: Israel sang praises, then complained three days later. What helps you remember God's past faithfulness when new trouble comes?

16.summary: In the wilderness of Sin the people grumble for food, longing for Egypt's meat pots; God sends quail in the evening and manna each morning, with instructions to gather only enough for each day and a double portion before the Sabbath; some disobey, and the extra rots; a jar of manna is kept as a memorial.
16.lookfor: Notice the rules about gathering, and the lesson of the Sabbath.

names.name: Sin
names.gloss: A wilderness between Elim and Sinai; the name is not the English word.

names.name: Sinai
names.gloss: The mountain region ahead.

insights.title: Meat pots of Egypt
insights.body: We sat by the meat pots and ate bread to the full (16:3). Slavery is remembered as a buffet; nostalgia rewrites the past.

insights.title: Manna
insights.body: When the Israelites saw it, they asked, what is it? (16:15). In Hebrew, man hu, which gave the name manna. It tasted like wafers with honey (16:31).

insights.title: Daily bread
insights.body: Gather a day's portion every day, that I may test them (16:4). Anything kept overnight bred worms. Israel learned to trust God one day at a time.

insights.title: Enough for everyone
insights.body: He who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack (16:18). Paul uses this to teach sharing among churches.

insights.title: Sabbath before Sinai
insights.body: On the sixth day they gather double, and on the seventh none falls (16:22-26). The Sabbath is practiced here before the Ten Commandments are given.

insights.title: Bread from heaven
insights.body: Jesus says he is the true bread from heaven: your fathers ate manna and died, but whoever eats this bread will live forever.

insights.title: Forty years
insights.body: Israel ate manna forty years, until they came to Canaan (16:35). Moses later explains: to teach that man doesn't live by bread alone.

insights.title: Enough for today
insights.body: God gave enough manna for each day, not a stockpile. What would it look like to trust God for today's needs?

17.summary: At Rephidim the thirsty people quarrel with Moses and test God, and God tells Moses to strike the rock at Horeb, from which water flows; the place is named Massah and Meribah; then Amalek attacks, and Israel prevails as long as Moses holds up his hands, supported by Aaron and Hur, while Joshua leads the fighting.
17.lookfor: Notice the people's question, and how Moses is helped when he grows tired.

names.name: Rephidim
names.gloss: A camp in the wilderness with no water.

names.name: Massah
names.gloss: Testing.

names.name: Meribah
names.gloss: Quarreling.

names.name: Amalek
names.gloss: A desert people descended from Esau, Israel's first attacker.

names.name: Joshua
names.gloss: Moses' young assistant, later his successor.

names.name: Hur
names.gloss: A leader who held up Moses' hands with Aaron.

insights.title: Is Yahweh among us?
insights.body: They tested Yahweh, saying, is Yahweh among us or not? (17:7). After every miracle so far, the question is still there. Psalm 95 warns later generations not to harden hearts as at Meribah.

insights.title: The rock was Christ
insights.body: Moses strikes the rock, and water comes out (17:6). Paul says they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ, struck so life could flow.

insights.title: Amalek's attack
insights.body: Amalek came and fought with Israel (17:8). Deuteronomy says they attacked the weary stragglers at the rear, a cowardly strike on the weak.

insights.title: Held-up hands
insights.body: When Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; when he let it down, Amalek prevailed (17:11). Aaron and Hur sat him on a stone and held up his hands until sunset.

insights.title: Joshua
insights.body: Joshua appears here for the first time (17:9). His name means Yahweh saves; in Greek it is Jesus.

insights.title: Yahweh is my banner
insights.body: Moses builds an altar and names it Yahweh Nissi, Yahweh is my banner (17:15). A banner was raised for troops to rally around; God himself is Israel's rallying point.

insights.title: Holding up hands
insights.body: Moses couldn't keep his arms up alone. Whose hands could you help hold up, and who holds up yours?

18.summary: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brings Moses' wife and sons to him, rejoices at what God has done, and offers sacrifices; seeing Moses judging the people alone from morning to evening, Jethro advises him to appoint capable, trustworthy leaders over groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, and Moses does so.
18.lookfor: Notice a foreign priest praising Yahweh, and his practical wisdom.

names.name: Jethro
names.gloss: Priest of Midian, Moses' father-in-law.

names.name: Zipporah
names.gloss: Moses' wife.

names.name: Gershom
names.gloss: Moses' son.

names.name: Eliezer
names.gloss: Moses' second son; my God is help.

insights.title: Jethro rejoiced
insights.body: Jethro rejoiced for all the goodness Yahweh had done to Israel and said, now I know that Yahweh is greater than all gods (18:9-11). A Midianite priest confesses Israel's God.

insights.title: Telling the story
insights.body: Moses told his father-in-law all that Yahweh had done to Pharaoh (18:8). Testimony leads to worship.

insights.title: It's not good
insights.body: The thing you're doing is not good; you'll wear yourself out, and the people too (18:17-18). Doing everything yourself isn't faithfulness; it's unsustainable.

insights.title: Qualities of leaders
insights.body: Choose able men who fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain (18:21). Character first, as in Paul's lists for elders.

insights.title: Thousands to tens
insights.body: Leaders of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens (18:21). Small groups with leaders who know them. Hard cases go to Moses; small ones are handled locally.

insights.title: Moses listened
insights.body: Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all he said (18:24). The great prophet humbly takes advice from an outsider.

insights.title: Sharing the load
insights.body: Jethro saw Moses doing too much alone. What load are you carrying that you should share with others?

19.summary: Three months after leaving Egypt, Israel camps at Sinai; God offers a covenant: if they obey, they will be his treasured possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation; the people agree, consecrate themselves for three days, and Yahweh descends on the mountain in fire, smoke, thunder and trumpet blast as the mountain trembles.
19.lookfor: Notice God's words about eagles' wings, and the awe and fear at the mountain.

names.name: Sinai
names.gloss: The mountain where God gave the covenant.

insights.title: Eagles' wings
insights.body: You've seen how I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself (19:4). The goal of the exodus wasn't just freedom from Egypt but nearness to God.

insights.title: A kingdom of priests
insights.body: You shall be my own possession among all peoples, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation (19:5-6). Israel was to represent God to the nations. Peter applies the same words to the church.

insights.title: Treasured possession
insights.body: The Hebrew segullah means a king's personal treasure, distinct from the royal estate (19:5). All the earth is his, but Israel is his special treasure.

insights.title: Grace before law
insights.body: God first reminds them what he has done (19:4), then gives the covenant. Obedience is a response to rescue, not a way to earn it.

insights.title: Boundaries
insights.body: Set bounds around the mountain; whoever touches it will die (19:12). God's holiness is dangerous for sinners to approach unprepared.

insights.title: Fire, cloud and trumpet
insights.body: Thunder, lightning, a thick cloud, a very loud trumpet, smoke like a furnace, and the whole mountain quaking (19:16-18). At Pentecost, the Spirit came with wind and fire, and many saw a new Sinai.

insights.title: Brought to himself
insights.body: God says he rescued Israel to bring them to himself. What does it mean to you that God's goal is closeness with you?

20.summary: God speaks the Ten Commandments to all Israel, beginning with his saving act: no other gods, no idols, honoring his name, keeping the Sabbath, honoring parents, and forbidding murder, adultery, theft, false witness and coveting; the terrified people ask Moses to speak to them instead; God gives instructions for a simple altar.
20.lookfor: Notice the first words before the commands, and the two groups of commands: toward God and toward neighbor.

insights.title: I brought you out
insights.body: I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage (20:2). The commandments begin with grace; they are the shape of life for a freed people.

insights.title: Ten words
insights.body: The Bible calls them the ten words (34:28). They were written on two tablets, perhaps two copies of the whole covenant, as ancient treaties gave each party a copy.

insights.title: No images
insights.body: You shall not make for yourselves an idol (20:4). Every neighboring nation worshiped images; Israel's God couldn't be captured in wood or stone.

insights.title: In vain
insights.body: You shall not take Yahweh's name in vain (20:7). More than avoiding swearing: don't use God's name emptily, falsely, or to back up lies.

insights.title: Rest for all
insights.body: The Sabbath rest includes your son, your daughter, your servants, your animals and the foreigner (20:10). In a world of endless work, even slaves got a day off.

insights.title: Love sums it up
insights.body: Jesus summed up the law in two commands: love God and love your neighbor. The first four commandments concern God; the last six concern neighbors.

insights.title: Don't covet
insights.body: You shall not covet (20:17). The last commandment reaches the heart, not just actions; Paul says it was this command that showed him his sin.

insights.title: Which one?
insights.body: Read the commands slowly. Which one is God putting his finger on in your life right now?

21.summary: God gives laws for Israel's society: limits on servitude with release in the seventh year, protections for female servants, penalties for murder, kidnapping, striking or cursing parents, and injuries, the principle of eye for eye, and responsibility for dangerous animals.
21.lookfor: Notice how these laws limit harm and protect the vulnerable compared with the ancient world.

insights.title: Case law
insights.body: Chapters 21 to 23 are called the Book of the Covenant (24:7). Like the older Code of Hammurabi, they use if-then cases; but Israel's laws value human life more highly than property.

insights.title: Release in the seventh year
insights.body: A Hebrew servant serves six years and goes free in the seventh (21:2). Servitude for debt was limited, not permanent.

insights.title: The pierced ear
insights.body: A servant who loves his master may choose to stay; his ear is pierced at the doorpost as a sign (21:5-6). Service by choice and love.

insights.title: Eye for eye
insights.body: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth (21:24). This limited revenge: punishment must fit the crime, no more. Judges applied it, often through compensation. Jesus calls his followers beyond it, to not retaliate.

insights.title: Kidnapping
insights.body: Anyone who kidnaps a person, whether he sells him or keeps him, shall be put to death (21:16). Paul lists manstealers among the lawless.

insights.title: Protecting slaves
insights.body: A master who knocks out a slave's eye or tooth must set him free (21:26-27). Unusual protection for slaves in the ancient world.

insights.title: Justice in daily life
insights.body: God's covenant reaches into ordinary disputes: injuries, animals, debts. Holiness isn't only worship; it's how a society treats people.

insights.title: Justice for the vulnerable
insights.body: These laws protected servants and the vulnerable. Who are the vulnerable people around you, and how could you protect them?

22.summary: Laws continue on theft and restitution, damage to crops and property, borrowed goods, seduction, sorcery and idolatry, and protection of foreigners, widows, orphans and the poor, forbidding interest on loans to the needy, along with commands to honor God with firstfruits.
22.lookfor: Notice God's personal concern for the widow, the orphan and the foreigner.

insights.title: Restitution
insights.body: A thief pays back double, or four or five times for a slaughtered ox or sheep (22:1-4). Israel's law aimed at making the victim whole, not at prison.

insights.title: You were foreigners
insights.body: You shall not wrong or oppress a foreigner, for you were foreigners in Egypt (22:21). Israel's own history of oppression grounds its ethics of compassion.

insights.title: I will hear their cry
insights.body: If you afflict a widow or orphan and they cry to me, I will surely hear their cry, and my wrath will burn (22:23-24). God takes the side of the defenseless.

insights.title: The cloak at sunset
insights.body: If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, return it by sunset; it's his only covering to sleep in (22:26-27). The poor often had one cloak, used as a blanket at night.

insights.title: No interest
insights.body: If you lend money to the poor, don't charge interest (22:25). Loans to the needy were meant as help, not profit.

insights.title: I am gracious
insights.body: When he cries to me, I will hear, for I am gracious (22:27). The law rests on God's character.

insights.title: Holy people
insights.body: You shall be holy men to me (22:31). Holiness covers worship and also how you treat the poor and the borrowed ox.

insights.title: The cloak at night
insights.body: God cared whether a poor man had a blanket at night. What small practical kindness could you show someone in need this week?

23.summary: Laws require honest testimony and impartial justice, even toward enemies' animals; a sabbath rest for the land every seventh year and for people every seventh day; three yearly feasts; and God promises an angel to guard Israel and bring them into the land, driving out its peoples little by little.
23.lookfor: Notice the command about an enemy's donkey, and why the land is conquered gradually.

names.name: Egypt
names.gloss: Whose memory shapes Israel's compassion.

insights.title: Don't follow the crowd
insights.body: Don't follow a multitude to do evil, nor twist justice to side with the majority (23:2). Truth isn't decided by the crowd.

insights.title: Your enemy's donkey
insights.body: If you meet your enemy's ox or donkey going astray, bring it back to him (23:4). Kindness to enemies is in the law; Jesus takes it further: love your enemies.

insights.title: A sabbath for the land
insights.body: Six years sow your land, and the seventh let it rest, so the poor may eat (23:10-11). Fallow years renewed soil and fed the needy.

insights.title: Three feasts
insights.body: Three times a year keep a feast: Unleavened Bread, Harvest (later Pentecost) and Ingathering (Tabernacles) (23:14-16). Pilgrimages tied Israel's calendar to God's saving acts and the harvest.

insights.title: A kid in its mother's milk
insights.body: You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk (23:19). Perhaps opposing a pagan ritual, or simply a lesson in compassion. Jewish tradition built its separation of meat and dairy on this verse.

insights.title: My angel
insights.body: I send an angel before you, to keep you by the way; my name is in him (23:20-21). This mysterious angel bears God's own name and authority.

insights.title: Little by little
insights.body: I won't drive them out in one year, lest the land become desolate; little by little I will drive them out (23:29-30). God's timing protects his people from more than they can handle.

insights.title: Little by little
insights.body: God promised gradual progress, not instant victory. Where do you need patience with slow growth?

24.summary: Moses reads the Book of the Covenant to the people, who promise to obey, and seals the covenant by sprinkling blood on the altar and people; Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders see the God of Israel and eat and drink; Moses goes up the mountain into the cloud for forty days.
24.lookfor: Notice the blood of the covenant, and the meal in God's presence.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Moses' brother.

names.name: Nadab
names.gloss: Aaron's son, who saw God.

names.name: Abihu
names.gloss: Aaron's son.

names.name: Joshua
names.gloss: Moses' assistant, who went partway up.

names.name: Hur
names.gloss: Left in charge with Aaron.

insights.title: We will do
insights.body: All the words Yahweh has spoken we will do (24:3, 24:7). Promised twice; broken within weeks at the golden calf.

insights.title: The blood of the covenant
insights.body: Moses sprinkles blood on the people: behold, the blood of the covenant (24:8). Jesus' words at the Last Supper echo it: this is my blood of the new covenant.

insights.title: A covenant meal
insights.body: They saw God, and ate and drank (24:11). Ancient treaties were sealed with a shared meal. The leaders eat in God's presence and live.

insights.title: A pavement of sapphire
insights.body: Under his feet was like a paved work of sapphire stone, like the sky itself (24:10). The description stops at his feet; no one describes God's face.

insights.title: Like devouring fire
insights.body: The glory of Yahweh looked like a devouring fire on the mountaintop to the Israelites (24:17).

insights.title: Forty days
insights.body: Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights (24:18), receiving the tabernacle plans. Forty again marks a time of meeting God.

insights.title: Written down
insights.body: Moses wrote all Yahweh's words (24:4). The covenant becomes a written text, the start of Scripture as a written book.

insights.title: Promises
insights.body: Israel promised wholehearted obedience and soon failed. What does it mean to you that the new covenant rests on Christ's faithfulness, not ours?

25.summary: God asks for willing offerings of gold, fabrics, wood, oil and stones so that Israel can make him a sanctuary to dwell among them, built exactly to the pattern shown; he gives instructions for the ark of the covenant with its mercy seat and cherubim, the table for bread, and the golden lampstand.
25.lookfor: Notice the purpose of the tabernacle in verse 8, and the ark's lid, the mercy seat.

skim.advice: Most of this chapter is detailed measurements; read verses 1 to 9 and 17 to 22 closely and skim the rest.

insights.title: Willing hearts
insights.body: Take an offering from everyone whose heart makes him willing (25:2). The sanctuary is built from free gifts, much of it gold received from the Egyptians.

insights.title: That I may dwell among them
insights.body: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them (25:8). The goal of the exodus: God living with his people, as in Eden. John says the Word became flesh and tabernacled among us.

insights.title: The pattern
insights.body: Make it according to the pattern I show you (25:9, 25:40). Hebrews says the earthly tabernacle was a copy and shadow of the heavenly one.

insights.title: The ark
insights.body: A chest of acacia wood overlaid with gold, about 4 feet long, carried on poles (25:10-15). It held the covenant tablets. Egyptian shrines were also carried on poles.

insights.title: The mercy seat
insights.body: The ark's gold lid, the mercy seat or atonement cover, with two cherubim facing each other (25:17-20). There, between the cherubim, God would meet with Moses (25:22). Paul uses the word for Christ.

insights.title: Bread of the presence
insights.body: Set bread of the presence on the table before me always (25:30). Twelve loaves for twelve tribes, a constant sign of fellowship.

insights.title: A lampstand like a tree
insights.body: The golden lampstand has branches, buds and almond blossoms (25:31-36), like a stylized tree, perhaps recalling the tree of life in Eden.

insights.title: God with us
insights.body: God asked for a tent so he could live among his people. How does God's desire to be near you change the way you think about him?

26.summary: God gives detailed instructions for the tabernacle structure: ten inner curtains of fine linen with cherubim, a covering of goat hair, coverings of rams' skins and fine leather, a frame of acacia boards with silver bases, and a veil separating the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place where the ark stands.
26.lookfor: Notice the layers of coverings, and the veil that divides the holy from the most holy.

skim.advice: This chapter is building specifications; skim the measurements and read about the veil in verses 31 to 35.

insights.title: A portable tent
insights.body: The tabernacle was a tent-shrine about 45 feet long and 15 wide, designed to be taken apart and carried. Egyptian portable shrines and royal campaign tents had similar frames and coverings.

insights.title: Cherubim woven in
insights.body: The inner curtains are woven with cherubim (26:1). Inside, priests were surrounded by images of the heavenly guardians, as cherubim guarded Eden.

insights.title: Plain outside, glorious inside
insights.body: The outer coverings are rams' skins and fine leather (26:14), plain to look at; inside is gold and colored linen. Isaiah's servant had no beauty that we should desire him.

insights.title: The veil
insights.body: The veil will separate the holy place from the most holy (26:33). Only the high priest could pass it, once a year.

insights.title: Torn in two
insights.body: When Jesus died, the temple veil was torn in two from top to bottom. Hebrews says we now enter the holy place through the veil, his flesh.

insights.title: Holiness and nearness
insights.body: The tabernacle sets God in the middle of the camp yet behind layers of curtains. He is near, but holy. The whole structure teaches both.

insights.title: Access
insights.body: Once only one man could enter God's presence once a year. How does access to God through Christ change your prayer life?

27.summary: God gives instructions for the bronze altar of burnt offering with horns at its corners, the outer courtyard with linen hangings on bronze posts and a colorful gate, and commands that pure olive oil be brought for the lamp to burn continually before Yahweh.
27.lookfor: Notice the altar as the first thing one meets entering, and the lamp that never goes out.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Who would tend the lamp.

skim.advice: Most of this chapter is measurements; read about the altar and the lamp.

insights.title: The bronze altar
insights.body: An altar of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, about 7.5 feet square and 4.5 high (27:1). Sacrifices burned here at the entrance: no one approached God except through sacrifice.

insights.title: Horns of the altar
insights.body: Make horns on its four corners (27:2). Blood was smeared on them in sin offerings, and a person fleeing for their life might cling to them for sanctuary.

insights.title: One gate
insights.body: The courtyard has one gate, about 30 feet wide, with colorful embroidered hangings (27:16). One way in. Jesus said, I am the door.

insights.title: Bronze outside, gold inside
insights.body: Bronze in the courtyard, silver bases, gold inside: the materials grow more precious closer to God's presence.

insights.title: The lamp continually
insights.body: Pure olive oil for the light, to make a lamp burn continually (27:20). Samuel heard God's call before the lamp of God went out.

insights.title: Approaching God
insights.body: From gate to altar to holy place to most holy place, the tabernacle maps the way to God: sacrifice, cleansing, light, presence.

insights.title: A lamp that stays lit
insights.body: The lamp was to burn continually. What keeps your devotion burning day after day?

28.summary: God commands holy garments for Aaron and his sons: an ephod with shoulder stones bearing the tribes' names, a breastpiece with twelve stones and the Urim and Thummim for judgment, a blue robe with bells and pomegranates, a turban with a gold plate engraved HOLY TO YAHWEH, and linen garments for the priests.
28.lookfor: Notice how the high priest carries the names of Israel on his shoulders and heart.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Israel's first high priest.

skim.advice: Much of this chapter describes the garments in detail; read verses 1 to 4, 9 to 12, 29 to 30 and 36 to 38.

insights.title: For glory and beauty
insights.body: Make holy garments for Aaron, for glory and for beauty (28:2). Worship involves beauty, not just function.

insights.title: Names on his shoulders
insights.body: Two onyx stones engraved with the names of Israel's sons sit on the ephod's shoulders, a memorial before Yahweh (28:12). The priest carries the people before God.

insights.title: Names on his heart
insights.body: Aaron bears the names of Israel on the breastpiece over his heart when he goes into the holy place (28:29). Hebrews says Jesus, our high priest, bears us before God.

insights.title: Urim and Thummim
insights.body: Put the Urim and Thummim in the breastpiece (28:30). These were likely used like lots to receive yes or no answers from God. Their exact form is unknown.

insights.title: Bells
insights.body: Golden bells on the robe's hem, so the sound is heard when he goes in and comes out, so he doesn't die (28:35). The people outside could hear their priest still serving in God's presence.

insights.title: Holy to Yahweh
insights.body: A gold plate on the turban engraved HOLY TO YAHWEH (28:36). Zechariah foresaw a day when even horses' bells and cooking pots would say it.

insights.title: Bearing guilt
insights.body: Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things (28:38). The priest stands between people and God, carrying their failures. Christ is the perfect high priest who bore our sins.

insights.title: Carried on his heart
insights.body: The high priest carried his people's names over his heart. How does it feel to know Christ carries your name before God?

29.summary: God gives the ceremony for ordaining Aaron and his sons as priests over seven days: washing, clothing, anointing, sin and burnt offerings, and the ram of ordination whose blood is put on the right ear, thumb and big toe; he commands daily morning and evening lamb offerings and promises to dwell among Israel and be their God.
29.lookfor: Notice the blood on ear, hand and foot, and God's promise at the end.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Ordained as high priest with his sons.

skim.advice: Much of this chapter describes the ordination rituals step by step; read verses 1 to 9, 19 to 21 and 38 to 46.

insights.title: Washed
insights.body: Bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tent of meeting and wash them with water (29:4). Cleansing comes before serving.

insights.title: Ear, thumb and toe
insights.body: Blood is put on the right ear, right thumb and right big toe (29:20): what they hear, what they do, where they go, all consecrated to God.

insights.title: Consecrate
insights.body: The Hebrew for ordain is literally fill the hand (29:9): the priests' hands are filled with offerings and with authority to serve.

insights.title: Seven days
insights.body: Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and sanctify it (29:37). A full week of preparation mirrors creation: a new beginning for worship.

insights.title: Morning and evening
insights.body: One lamb in the morning, the other at evening, a continual offering (29:38-42). The early church kept prayer at the hour of the evening offering.

insights.title: I will dwell among them
insights.body: I will dwell among the children of Israel and be their God; they will know that I am Yahweh their God who brought them out of Egypt, that I might dwell among them (29:45-46). The exodus was for this: God living with his people.

insights.title: Consecrated
insights.body: The priests' ears, hands and feet were set apart for God. What would it look like for your hearing, doing and going to be dedicated to him?

30.summary: God gives instructions for the golden altar of incense before the veil, a half-shekel ransom paid by every man counted in the census, a bronze basin for priests to wash, the holy anointing oil, and the sacred incense, which must not be copied for personal use.
30.lookfor: Notice that rich and poor pay the same ransom, and the incense that rises continually.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Who burns incense morning and evening.

skim.advice: This chapter is mostly instructions for objects and recipes; read verses 1 to 10, 11 to 16 and 17 to 21.

insights.title: The altar of incense
insights.body: A small golden altar stood before the veil, burning incense morning and evening (30:1-8). Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, was serving here when the angel appeared.

insights.title: Incense and prayer
insights.body: Incense rising before God became a picture of prayer. Revelation shows golden bowls of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

insights.title: Same price for all
insights.body: The rich shall not give more and the poor not less than half a shekel (30:15). Every life is redeemed at the same price; no one is worth more before God.

insights.title: The temple tax
insights.body: This half-shekel became the annual temple tax in Jesus' day; Peter paid it for himself and Jesus with a coin from a fish's mouth.

insights.title: Wash before serving
insights.body: Priests must wash hands and feet at the bronze basin before entering, so they don't die (30:20-21). Constant reminders that God is holy.

insights.title: Anointing oil
insights.body: The holy anointing oil of myrrh, cinnamon, calamus and cassia (30:23-25) set apart priests and objects. Messiah and Christ both mean anointed one.

insights.title: Holy and not common
insights.body: The incense and oil must not be copied for ordinary use (30:32-38). Holy means set apart for God; some things must never be treated as common.

insights.title: Prayer like incense
insights.body: Incense burned morning and evening before God. What could a morning and evening rhythm of prayer look like for you?

31.summary: God names Bezalel of Judah and Oholiab of Dan, filling Bezalel with his Spirit and skill to make the tabernacle and its furnishings; he commands the Sabbath as a lasting sign of the covenant; and he gives Moses the two tablets of the testimony written by the finger of God.
31.lookfor: Notice the first person said to be filled with God's Spirit, and why.

names.name: Bezalel
names.gloss: A craftsman of Judah filled with God's Spirit; the name means in God's shadow.

names.name: Hur
names.gloss: Bezalel's grandfather.

names.name: Judah
names.gloss: Bezalel's tribe.

names.name: Oholiab
names.gloss: A craftsman of Dan, Bezalel's helper.

names.name: Dan
names.gloss: Oholiab's tribe.

insights.title: Filled with the Spirit
insights.body: I have filled Bezalel with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all kinds of workmanship (31:3). The first person in the Bible said to be filled with God's Spirit is an artist.

insights.title: Art and skill
insights.body: Bezalel designs artistic works in gold, silver and bronze, cuts stones, and carves wood (31:4-5). Craft and beauty are gifts of God's Spirit.

insights.title: Two tribes
insights.body: Bezalel from Judah, a leading tribe, and Oholiab from Dan, a lesser one (31:2, 31:6). God gifts people across the whole community.

insights.title: A sign forever
insights.body: The Sabbath is a sign between me and you, that you may know I am Yahweh who sanctifies you (31:13). Rest itself is a mark of belonging to God.

insights.title: Even while building
insights.body: The Sabbath command comes right after the building instructions (31:12-17). Even work for God must stop for rest.

insights.title: The finger of God
insights.body: Two tablets of stone, written with the finger of God (31:18). God's own hand writes the covenant. Paul contrasts this with the Spirit writing on hearts.

insights.title: Your skill
insights.body: God filled an artisan with his Spirit to make beautiful things. What skill or craft could you offer to God's service?

32.summary: While Moses delays on the mountain, the people demand gods and Aaron makes a golden calf, which they worship with feasting; God tells Moses he will destroy them, but Moses pleads and God relents; Moses comes down, breaks the tablets, burns the calf, and the Levites carry out judgment; Moses offers to be blotted out of God's book for the people.
32.lookfor: Notice Aaron's excuses, Moses' intercession, and his offer to die for the people.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Who made the calf.

names.name: Joshua
names.gloss: Who mistook the noise for war.

names.name: Levi
names.gloss: The tribe that rallied to Moses.

insights.title: A calf
insights.body: Aaron makes a molten calf, and they say, these are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of Egypt (32:4). Bulls symbolized strength and fertility in Egypt and Canaan; some think the calf was meant as Yahweh's pedestal, but it broke the second commandment.

insights.title: A feast to Yahweh
insights.body: Aaron proclaims, tomorrow shall be a feast to Yahweh (32:5). They didn't think they were abandoning God, just reshaping him to fit their liking.

insights.title: Moses pleads
insights.body: Moses reminds God of his reputation among the Egyptians and his promises to Abraham, Isaac and Israel (32:11-13). Yahweh relents (32:14). Intercession appeals to God's own character and word.

insights.title: It came out
insights.body: Aaron says, I threw the gold into the fire, and out came this calf (32:24). One of the Bible's lamest excuses.

insights.title: Breaking the tablets
insights.body: Moses throws down the tablets and breaks them at the foot of the mountain (32:19). The covenant was broken before it was even delivered.

insights.title: Blot me out
insights.body: Forgive their sin, or else blot me out of your book (32:32). Moses offers himself in their place. Paul would later wish himself cut off for his people; Christ actually took our place.

insights.title: Who is on Yahweh's side?
insights.body: Moses calls, whoever is on Yahweh's side, come to me, and the Levites gather to him (32:26). Their loyalty becomes the reason they're set apart for priestly service.

insights.title: Reshaping God
insights.body: Israel made a god they could see and control. In what ways are you tempted to reshape God into something more comfortable?

33.summary: God says he will send an angel but won't go with them himself, lest he destroy them; the people mourn and remove their ornaments; Moses meets God face to face in the tent of meeting, pleads for God's presence to go with them, and asks to see his glory; God promises to pass by, hiding Moses in a cleft of the rock.
33.lookfor: Notice Moses' refusal to go without God, and the request to see his glory.

names.name: Joshua
names.gloss: Who stayed in the tent of meeting.

names.name: Horeb
names.gloss: Sinai, where the people stripped off their ornaments.

insights.title: The land without God?
insights.body: God offers the land, an angel and victory, but not his presence (33:2-3). The people mourn (33:4). The best gifts without God himself aren't worth having.

insights.title: The tent of meeting
insights.body: Moses pitched a tent outside the camp, and the pillar of cloud came down at its door (33:7-9). This was a temporary meeting place before the tabernacle was built.

insights.title: Face to face
insights.body: Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend (33:11). Intimacy with God, as a friend.

insights.title: If your presence doesn't go
insights.body: If your presence doesn't go with us, don't carry us up from here (33:15). What sets Israel apart from all other nations is God's presence, nothing else.

insights.title: Show me your glory
insights.body: Moses asks, please show me your glory (33:18). God replies, I will make all my goodness pass before you and proclaim my name (33:19). God's glory is his goodness.

insights.title: No one can see my face
insights.body: You can't see my face, for man may not see me and live (33:20). John says no one has seen God; the only Son has made him known.

insights.title: The cleft of the rock
insights.body: I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand while I pass by; you'll see my back (33:22-23). Elijah later stands at the same mountain cave as God passes by.

insights.title: Presence over gifts
insights.body: Moses refused God's gifts without God's presence. Do you want God's blessings more than you want God himself?

34.summary: Moses cuts two new tablets, and Yahweh descends and proclaims his name: merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving kindness and truth, forgiving yet not clearing the guilty; God renews the covenant with warnings against idolatry; Moses comes down with his face shining and veils it.
34.lookfor: Notice God's description of himself in verses 6 and 7, quoted throughout the Old Testament.

names.name: Sinai
names.gloss: The mountain of the covenant.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: Whose face shone after speaking with God.

insights.title: New tablets
insights.body: Cut two tablets of stone like the first (34:1). God gives a second chance after the covenant was broken.

insights.title: God's own name
insights.body: Yahweh, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth, keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity (34:6-7). God's self-description after the golden calf: mercy first.

insights.title: Loving kindness
insights.body: Hesed, loving kindness or steadfast love, is covenant love that keeps faith even when the other party fails. It's at the heart of God's character.

insights.title: Not clearing the guilty
insights.body: He will by no means clear the guilty, visiting iniquity on children to the third and fourth generation (34:7). Mercy doesn't cancel justice; the consequences of sin ripple through families, but mercy reaches to thousands.

insights.title: Jealous
insights.body: Yahweh, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God (34:14). Not petty envy, but the exclusive love of a husband who won't share his bride with rivals.

insights.title: A shining face
insights.body: Moses didn't know that his face shone because he had been speaking with God (34:29). He veiled it; Paul says believers now reflect the Lord's glory with unveiled faces.

insights.title: He didn't know
insights.body: Moses was unaware of his own glowing face (34:29). Time with God changes us in ways others notice before we do.

insights.title: Who God says he is
insights.body: When God described himself, he led with mercy and grace. Which part of verses 6 and 7 do you most need to believe today?

35.summary: Moses repeats the Sabbath command, then asks for willing offerings for the tabernacle; men and women whose hearts are stirred bring gold, jewelry, fabrics and skills, and skilled women spin; Moses announces that God has filled Bezalel and Oholiab with skill and the ability to teach.
35.lookfor: Notice how often the words willing and stirred appear, and the women's contributions.

names.name: Bezalel
names.gloss: The master craftsman from Judah.

names.name: Oholiab
names.gloss: Bezalel's partner from Dan.

insights.title: Sabbath first
insights.body: Before the building begins, Moses repeats: six days work, but the seventh day is a holy Sabbath (35:2). Even God's work must stop for rest.

insights.title: Whose heart stirred him
insights.body: Everyone whose heart stirred him and whose spirit made him willing brought an offering (35:21). The tabernacle is built from voluntary love.

insights.title: From the calf to the tabernacle
insights.body: Gold that was melted into a calf in chapter 32 is now freely given for God's dwelling (35:22). The same people, a different heart.

insights.title: Women who spun
insights.body: All the wise-hearted women spun with their hands and brought what they had spun: blue, purple, scarlet and fine linen, and goats' hair (35:25-26). Women's skilled work is woven into the sanctuary.

insights.title: Gifted to teach
insights.body: God put in Bezalel's heart that he may teach, he and Oholiab (35:34). Gifts are meant to be passed on.

insights.title: Everyone involved
insights.body: Rulers bring stones, women spin, craftsmen build (35:25-35). The dwelling place of God is a project of the whole community.

insights.title: A stirred heart
insights.body: The people gave because their hearts were stirred. What is God stirring your heart to give right now?

36.summary: The craftsmen begin work, but the people keep bringing so much that Moses has to tell them to stop; Bezalel's team makes the tabernacle's curtains, coverings, frames and the veil, exactly as commanded.
36.lookfor: Notice the remarkable problem of too much giving, then skim the building details.

names.name: Bezalel
names.gloss: Who led the work.

names.name: Oholiab
names.gloss: Who worked with him.

skim.advice: Verses 8 to 38 repeat the instructions of chapter 26 as they are carried out; skim them.

insights.title: Too much
insights.body: The people bring much more than enough for the work (36:5). Moses commands, let no one make anything else for the offering, so the people were restrained from bringing (36:6). A rare problem.

insights.title: Why repeat everything?
insights.body: Chapters 36 to 39 repeat almost word for word the instructions of 25 to 31, now as completed work. The repetition stresses exact obedience: they did everything as Yahweh commanded.

insights.title: Ancient building accounts
insights.body: Ancient Near Eastern temple-building texts also record instructions followed by a detailed account of their completion. Exodus uses a familiar form.

insights.title: Wise-hearted
insights.body: Every wise-hearted man, in whom Yahweh had put wisdom and understanding (36:1). In Hebrew, wisdom includes practical skill, not just knowledge.

insights.title: The veil made
insights.body: He made the veil of blue, purple, scarlet and fine linen, with cherubim (36:35). The same veil that would one day be torn from top to bottom.

insights.title: Generosity overflowing
insights.body: The people who grumbled for food now give until they're told to stop. Grace received becomes grace given.

insights.title: More than enough
insights.body: The Israelites gave so generously they had to be told to stop. What would overflowing generosity look like for you?

37.summary: Bezalel makes the ark of acacia wood overlaid with gold, the mercy seat with two cherubim, the table and its utensils, the golden lampstand with almond blossoms, the altar of incense, the anointing oil and the incense, all according to the pattern.
37.lookfor: Notice that Bezalel himself makes the most sacred object, the ark.

names.name: Bezalel
names.gloss: Who made the ark with his own hands.

skim.advice: This chapter repeats the instructions of chapters 25 and 30 as completed work; skim the details.

insights.title: Bezalel made the ark
insights.body: Bezalel made the ark (37:1). The chief craftsman personally makes the most sacred object.

insights.title: Cherubim facing each other
insights.body: The cherubim spread their wings above, their faces toward each other and toward the mercy seat (37:9). Peter says angels long to look into the salvation the mercy seat pictured.

insights.title: A talent of gold
insights.body: The lampstand and its accessories used a talent of pure gold (37:24), about 75 pounds. The sanctuary was lavish.

insights.title: Almond blossoms
insights.body: The lampstand's cups were shaped like almond blossoms (37:19). The almond tree blooms first in spring; its Hebrew name sounds like watchful. God watches over his word.

insights.title: Pure and holy
insights.body: The holy anointing oil and pure incense, the work of the perfumer (37:29). Everything near God's presence is made with care and purity.

insights.title: Faithful to the pattern
insights.body: Every piece follows God's design. The tabernacle points ahead to Christ, in whom God's presence, light, provision and atonement all meet.

insights.title: Care in small things
insights.body: Even the snuffers were made of pure gold. Where is God asking you to do ordinary tasks with excellence for him?

38.summary: Bezalel makes the bronze altar of burnt offering, the bronze basin from the mirrors of the women who served at the tent's entrance, and the courtyard with its hangings and gate; an inventory under Ithamar records the gold, silver and bronze used.
38.lookfor: Notice the women's mirrors, and the exact accounting of materials.

names.name: Bezalel
names.gloss: Who made all that Yahweh commanded.

names.name: Ithamar
names.gloss: Aaron's son, who supervised the inventory.

names.name: Oholiab
names.gloss: An engraver and embroiderer.

skim.advice: The second half of this chapter is an inventory of metals; read verses 8 and 21 to 25 and skim the rest.

insights.title: Mirrors into a basin
insights.body: He made the bronze basin from the mirrors of the serving women who served at the door of the tent of meeting (38:8). Polished bronze mirrors were precious; these women gave them up for washing before worship.

insights.title: Bronze mirrors
insights.body: Egyptian women prized polished bronze hand mirrors; many have been found in tombs. Giving one up was giving up something personal and valuable.

insights.title: Accountability
insights.body: This is the amount of the tabernacle, as counted at Moses' command, by the Levites under Ithamar (38:21). Even sacred gifts are recorded carefully.

insights.title: Silver from the census
insights.body: The silver came from the half-shekel ransom paid by 603,550 men (38:25-26). Every person counted contributed equally to the foundation sockets.

insights.title: The basin and washing
insights.body: The basin for washing stood between the altar and the tent (38:8). Priests washed before serving; Titus speaks of the washing of regeneration.

insights.title: Built on ransom
insights.body: The tabernacle's silver sockets, its foundations, were made from the ransom money (38:27). God's dwelling rests on redemption.

insights.title: Giving something personal
insights.body: The women gave their mirrors for the basin. What personal thing could you offer to God's purposes?

39.summary: The priestly garments are made exactly as commanded: the ephod, the breastpiece with twelve stones, the blue robe with bells and pomegranates, tunics, turbans and the gold plate engraved HOLY TO YAHWEH; all the work is completed and brought to Moses, who inspects it and blesses the people.
39.lookfor: Notice the refrain "as Yahweh commanded Moses," and Moses' blessing at the end.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: For whom the garments were made.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: Who inspected the work and blessed them.

skim.advice: This chapter repeats the instructions of chapter 28 as completed work; notice the refrain and read verses 32 to 43.

insights.title: As Yahweh commanded
