insights.body: The phrase as Yahweh commanded Moses appears seven times in this chapter (39:1, 39:5, 39:7, 39:21, 39:26, 39:29, 39:31). Complete, careful obedience.

insights.title: Echoes of creation
insights.body: All the work was finished; Moses saw all the work, and behold, they had done it; and Moses blessed them (39:32, 39:43). The wording echoes Genesis 1 and 2: God saw all he made, finished his work and blessed. The tabernacle is a new creation.

insights.title: Gold thread
insights.body: They beat gold into thin plates and cut it into threads to weave into the fabric (39:3). Egyptian craftsmen used the same technique.

insights.title: Holy to Yahweh
insights.body: They wrote on the plate, like a signet engraving, HOLY TO YAHWEH (39:30). The finished crown of the priestly garments.

insights.title: Moses inspects
insights.body: They brought the tabernacle to Moses (39:33), who checked everything against God's pattern. Faithful work invites inspection.

insights.title: Moses blessed them
insights.body: Moses blessed them (39:43). After the golden calf, the people are now blessed for faithful work. Restoration is complete.

insights.title: Finished work
insights.body: Moses saw that the people had done everything as commanded. What work has God given you to finish faithfully?

40.summary: On the first day of the first month of the second year, Moses sets up the tabernacle, places the ark, table, lampstand, altar and basin, and anoints and consecrates Aaron and his sons; when the work is finished, the cloud covers the tent and the glory of Yahweh fills it so that Moses can't enter; the cloud leads Israel on all their journeys.
40.lookfor: Notice the date, the refrain of obedience, and the glorious ending.

names.name: Moses
names.gloss: Who set up the tabernacle.

names.name: Aaron
names.gloss: Anointed and consecrated as priest.

insights.title: New Year's Day
insights.body: On the first day of the first month of the second year, the tabernacle was raised up (40:17). Almost exactly a year after the exodus, God's dwelling is set up on New Year's Day.

insights.title: Moses did everything
insights.body: Moses did so; according to all that Yahweh commanded him, so he did (40:16). The refrain as Yahweh commanded Moses rings seven more times.

insights.title: Moses finished the work
insights.body: So Moses finished the work (40:33), echoing God finishing the work of creation. Jesus, on the cross, said it is finished.

insights.title: The glory filled it
insights.body: The cloud covered the tent of meeting, and Yahweh's glory filled the tabernacle (40:34). God, who came down on Sinai, now dwells in the middle of the camp. The book that began with slavery ends with God's presence.

insights.title: Moses couldn't enter
insights.body: Moses wasn't able to enter, because the cloud stayed on it and the glory filled it (40:35). Even Moses must wait; Leviticus will explain how sinful people can approach.

insights.title: God's dwelling, then and now
insights.body: The tabernacle is fulfilled in Jesus, who tabernacled among us; in the church, God's temple; and finally in the new creation, where God's dwelling is with people.

insights.title: On all their journeys
insights.body: Whenever the cloud lifted, Israel set out; if it didn't lift, they stayed (40:36-37). God's presence guides the whole journey.

insights.title: God in the middle
insights.body: Exodus ends with God living in the middle of his people. What would it mean for God to be truly at the center of your life?

intro.who: Tradition credits Moses, who is said to have written down parts of it (17:14, 24:4). Many scholars think it was compiled from older sources over centuries.
intro.when: The events are dated to the 1400s BC by some and to the 1200s BC, under Pharaoh Rameses II, by many others. The writing is dated by tradition to Moses' lifetime and by many scholars to later centuries.
intro.why: Exodus means going out. It tells how God heard his enslaved people, revealed his name to Moses, rescued Israel from Egypt with mighty acts, made a covenant with them at Sinai, and came to live among them in the tabernacle. It's the Old Testament's great story of salvation.
